entities.name: Leotychidas II
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Leotychidas II, a king from the Eurypontid house of Sparta, reigned from 491 to 468 BCE, serving alongside Agiad kings Cleomenes I, Leonidas I, and Pleistarchus. His tenure was defined by the pivotal latter stages of the Greco-Persian Wars, where he emerged as a crucial military commander whose actions fundamentally shifted the balance of power in the Aegean Sea. His leadership was instrumental in securing Greek independence against the vast Achaemenid Empire, particularly through decisive naval and land engagements that marked the end of major Persian incursions into the Greek world.

His most celebrated achievement occurred in 479 BCE when, commanding the united Greek fleet and land forces, he orchestrated the crushing victory at the Battle of Mycale, fought simultaneously with the Battle of Plataea. This engagement, near the Ionian coast, saw the destruction of the Persian fleet and a significant portion of their land army, effectively ending Persian naval power in the Aegean. Following this triumph, Leotychidas led expeditions to liberate Greek cities in Ionia and the Hellespont and later campaigned in Thessaly against the pro-Persian Aleuadae. However, his career ended ignominiously; in 476 BCE, he was accused of accepting a bribe from the Aleuadae during his Thessalian campaign and fled into exile in Tegea, avoiding a Spartan trial.

The immediate consequence of Mycale, largely attributed to Leotychidas, was the permanent expulsion of the Achaemenid fleet from the Aegean, paving the way for the formation of the Athenian-led Delian League in 478 BCE. This shift initiated the period of Athenian hegemony and set the stage for the Peloponnesian War decades later, as Sparta's influence waned in the eastern Aegean. His exile, a stark reminder of Spartan political ruthlessness, left a power vacuum that saw the controversial rise and fall of his relative Pausanias, further destabilizing Spartan foreign policy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Leotychidas II's command at the Battle of Mycale in 479 BCE was a pivotal moment, irrevocably ending Persian naval dominance in the Aegean and directly enabling the rise of Athenian hegemony through the Delian League, thus reshaping the geopolitical landscape of Classical Greece.
